config.title: Star Rating Component

intro.title: Star Rating Component
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Star Rating Component that allows users to select a rating from one to five stars. You will learn how to use Angular's component structure and data binding to display interactive stars. The core programming concept involves handling user input events to update the component's state and reflect the selected rating visually. You will work with TypeScript for logic, Angular templates for the UI, and CSS for styling the stars. By the end, you'll have a functional component that can be integrated into any Angular application to collect user feedback.
intro.usecase: Star rating components are a fundamental UI pattern for collecting and displaying user feedback across countless applications. You'll implement them in e-commerce product pages, like on Amazon or eBay, to allow customers to rate items they've purchased. They are also essential in service review platforms, such as Yelp or TripAdvisor, where users rate restaurants or hotels, and in media apps like Netflix or Goodreads for rating movies or books. As a developer, you'll build these interactive components to enhance user engagement and provide valuable data for your application's analytics and recommendations.

objectives: Implement a reusable star rating component with TypeScript class and Angular decorators
Configure component input properties to control rating values and maximum stars
Bind click events to update the rating based on user interaction
Render dynamic star icons using Angular's template syntax and property binding
Apply CSS classes conditionally to display filled and empty star states
Integrate the star rating component into a parent component and pass data
Manipulate the component's appearance through style bindings and hover effects

steps.title: Import Component, Input, Output, and EventEmitter from @angular/core
steps.instruction: In the TypeScript file, import Component, Input, Output, and EventEmitter from '@angular/core'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple symbols from the Angular core module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing Angular core symbols
import { Component, Input, Output, EventEmitter } from '@angular/core';
steps.seedCode: // Import Component, Input, Output, and EventEmitter from '@angular/core' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The Angular core symbols needed for creating a component with data binding are imported.
successCriteria: Component, Input, Output, and EventEmitter are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some symbols, but make sure to include all four: Component, Input, Output, and EventEmitter from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. Import Component, Input, Output, and EventEmitter from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create the StarRatingComponent class with @Component decorator
steps.instruction: Define the StarRatingComponent class with the @Component decorator. Include the selector 'app-star-rating' and template URL './star-rating.component.html'.
steps.hint: Use the imported Component decorator to define the component metadata. The class should be named StarRatingComponent.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, Input, Output, EventEmitter } from '@angular/core';

// Define the StarRatingComponent class with @Component decorator here
steps.expectedOutcome: The StarRatingComponent class is defined with proper Angular component metadata.
successCriteria: StarRatingComponent class is defined with @Component decorator, selector 'app-star-rating', and templateUrl './star-rating.component.html'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've included the @Component decorator with both selector and templateUrl properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class isn't properly defined. Check that you're using the @Component decorator with the correct selector and templateUrl.

steps.title: Add Input property for current rating with type annotation
steps.instruction: Inside the StarRatingComponent class, add a rating input property with the @Input decorator and type it as number.
steps.hint: Use @Input() before the property name and add the type annotation with a colon and number.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a typed input property named rating that can receive a numeric value from a parent component.
successCriteria: The StarRatingComponent class contains a property named rating decorated with @Input() and typed as number.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the rating property, but check if it has the @Input decorator and the correct number type annotation.
steps.feedbackWrong: The rating input property is missing or incorrect. Make sure to use @Input() before the property name and add : number for the type.

steps.title: Add Input property for maximum stars with default value
steps.instruction: Add a maxStars input property with a default value of 5 to your StarRatingComponent class using the @Input decorator.
steps.hint: Use @Input() with a default value assignment in the property declaration.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Input property with default value
@Input() maxItems: number = 10;
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a maxStars input property that defaults to 5.
successCriteria: The StarRatingComponent class contains a maxStars property decorated with @Input and initialized to 5.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the property, but check the default value or the @Input decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The maxStars input property with default value is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Add Output property for rating change events
steps.instruction: Add a ratingChanged output property using the @Output decorator and EventEmitter<number> to your StarRatingComponent class.
steps.hint: Use @Output() ratingChanged = new EventEmitter<number>(); to declare an output that emits number values.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Output property in Angular
@Output() valueChanged = new EventEmitter<string>();
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an output property ready to emit rating change events.
successCriteria: The StarRatingComponent class contains a ratingChanged property decorated with @Output and initialized as new EventEmitter<number>().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've used both @Output() decorator and EventEmitter<number>().
steps.feedbackWrong: The ratingChanged output property is missing or incorrect. Check the syntax: @Output() ratingChanged = new EventEmitter<number>();

steps.title: Create the component template structure
steps.instruction: Add a template property to the @Component decorator with a container div element that will hold the stars.
steps.hint: The template property should be a string containing HTML. Start with a simple div that will serve as the wrapper for your star elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a basic template structure with a container div ready to hold star elements.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes a template property with a div element as the container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the template property to the @Component decorator with a div element inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template property is missing or incomplete. Add a template property to @Component with a div element as the container.

steps.title: Add ngFor loop to generate star elements
steps.instruction: Inside the component's template, add an *ngFor directive to iterate over a range from 1 to maxStars and generate a <span> element for each star.
steps.hint: Use Angular's *ngFor structural directive with a template variable. You can create an array of numbers using Array(maxStars).keys() and map it appropriately.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: generating list items
  • {{ item }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain an *ngFor directive that creates multiple <span> elements based on the maxStars property.
successCriteria: The *ngFor directive is correctly implemented with proper syntax, iterating from 1 to maxStars and generating a <span> for each iteration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check the *ngFor syntax and ensure you're iterating over the correct range.
steps.feedbackWrong: The *ngFor loop is missing or incorrect. Review Angular's *ngFor directive syntax and how to generate a range of numbers.

steps.title: Add click event binding to star elements
steps.instruction: In the template, add a (click) event binding to each star span that calls the setRating method with the star's index value.
steps.hint: Use (click)="setRating(i + 1)" inside the ngFor loop to make each star clickable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: binding click event to a button
<button (click)="handleClick()">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: Each star element will respond to clicks and update the rating when clicked.
successCriteria: The star spans have (click) event bindings that call setRating with the correct star value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added (click) event bindings to each star span inside the ngFor loop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The click event bindings aren't properly set up. Check that you've added (click)="setRating(i + 1)" to each star span.

steps.title: Add conditional class binding for star display
steps.instruction: Add a [class.filled] binding to the span element to conditionally apply the 'filled' CSS class when the star index is less than the current rating.
steps.hint: Use Angular's class binding syntax: [class.className]="condition". The condition should check if i < rating.
steps.expectedOutcome: The span element now has a conditional class binding that will apply the 'filled' CSS class when the star should be filled.
successCriteria: The span element includes [class.filled]="i < rating" binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the binding syntax is correct: [class.filled]="i < rating".
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional class binding wasn't added correctly. Review Angular's class binding syntax.
